estimate.damage_summary: An atmospheric overvoltage event damaged the speaker system and TV connected to the building’s electrical installation. The technician attended afterward to diagnose the surge failure and check the wiring.
estimate.policy_notes: Clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4 cover established physical damage to connected electrical appliances, subject to the EUR 5,000 VAT-inclusive aggregate appliance sub-limit and the no-improvement rule in 7.1.9. Because the description establishes that no surge-protective device was used, clause 2.3.3 halves the otherwise payable indemnity for the damaged appliances. Under 7.1.8 and operative clause 11.2, delivery and putting replacement equipment into service, diagnostics, arrangement/order charges and attendance accompanying non-indemnifiable work are not repair costs.

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: Clauses 2.3.3, 4.2.4 and 7.1.1 cover replacement of appliances with established surge damage, limited to the pre-loss standard under 7.1.9 and the appliance sub-limit; the description identifies the speaker system and TV as damaged. The line’s predominant stated purpose is replacement equipment, but any bundled delivery and putting-into-service charges are excluded by 7.1.8(b)–(c) and operative clause 11.2, so the threshold reflects standard-grade equipment only, not those ancillary charges.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: Although diagnosis relates to the reported event, operative clause 11.2 characterises the provider’s work as an arrangement and order under an equipment property/liability arrangement, excluded by 3.1.4, 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(f); the contractor’s own diagnostic report is also excluded by 7.1.8(e). Clause 7.1.8(d) excludes the associated attendance charge because the invoice’s underlying work is not indemnifiable, and the singular report/attendance does not support three separate units.
